graph.objects(subject=param, predicate=BRICK.aliasOf) is exactly this stratum's target: for one-step reads not written as a for-loop, list(m{ {param} brick:aliasOf ?o }) is the most specific construction available -- arity 1, {param} a term interpolated from a Python value. is_alias only tests len(...)==0, so this also exercises the fixture's zero-solution case (Min_Limit, Max_Limit have no brick:aliasOf) and one-solution case (Alias_Limit does).

@graph graph declared once at function entry captures the parameter's value; graph is never reassigned in this function so the capture stays valid for the whole body (see ldpy/012-class scoping caveat in INSTRUCTIONS.md 2 bis).

The static SELECT (qstr, assigned then passed unchanged to graph.query(qstr)) is directly expressible as s{ SELECT ?param WHERE { ?param rdfs:subClassOf* brick:Limit } }(graph); this is bonus beyond the assigned trav_one_step stratum but the most-specific-construction rule (INSTRUCTIONS.md 2) applies regardless of which stratum a region was sampled for.

NOT translated: graph.query(f"""select ?class where {{ BIND(brick:{setpoint} as ?class) ... }}""").bindings kept as a raw rdflib call. Tried s{ SELECT ?class WHERE { BIND(brick:{setpoint} as ?class) ... } } and it does not parse: LdpySyntaxError on the BIND. Per the reference table, s{ }'s {expr} interpolation fills a whole term position (an initial binding for a projected/bound variable) -- it is not string-pasting into a prefixed name's local part the way g{ }/m{ }/e<...> support since 0.4.0 (ex:{expr}). Building the class IRI in Python first (brick[setpoint]) and interpolating the whole term would change the query's variable-binding shape from the original's BIND-based one; since this read never reaches the triple store used to write the graph (class_exists only feeds a logging.warning, no RDF is added or removed from it), it was left as-is rather than risk a subtly different query. Signalled per INSTRUCTIONS.md 5, not a strata target of this batch.

repair.driver: Ce que la région journalise est comparé (un handler sur le logger racine imprime niveau et message, comparés comme stdout appel par appel) ; deux graphes de plus : les formes que le générateur du dépôt écrit (limites à deux et trois niveaux sous brick:Limit, une sous deux parents, un alias en profondeur avec owl:equivalentClass, une classe reliée par skos:broader seulement, un voisin owl:sameAs, une hiérarchie brick:Class qui contient certains setpoints inférés et pas d'autres) et la hiérarchie d'origine sans brick:Setpoint sous brick:Class (brick:Limit, atteint par le seul pas de longueur zéro de `*`, journalise alors son avertissement) ; trois CSV de cas écrits dans un répertoire temporaire où l'appel s'exécute (seeAlso sans définition, ligne à deux colonnes, terme répété, virgule entre guillemets ; ligne trop longue après une bonne -> ValueError, graphe partiel comparé ; en-tête seul). Les graphes lient leurs préfixes comme le G du dépôt (generate_brick.py:74) : la requête brute d'origine en dépend, s{ } et @graph non, et le dépôt ne l'appelle jamais sur un graphe sans liaisons.
repair.remaining: SELECT DISTINCT est un mutant équivalent (le chemin `*` de rdflib rend chaque paire une fois, même sous deux parents) : non compté. La question wrong-construction du tri (suffixe `(graph)` de s{ } redondant avec @graph graph) reste à juger.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the first SELECT (`?param rdfs:subClassOf* brick:Limit`) becomes `list(graph.subjects(RDFS.subClassOf * "*", BRICK.Limit))`: rdflib's SPARQL engine evaluates a one-pattern path through the same graph.triples() path evaluation, so the subjects come in the same order and with the same multiplicity (checked on the driver's three hierarchies); list() keeps the materialisation, since the loop adds to the graph it reads. Like translated.ldpy's s{ }, it no longer depends on the graph binding the brick:/rdfs: prefixes. The `is_alias` list becomes the existence test `(param, BRICK.aliasOf, None) not in graph`; the if/elif chain on the Min/Max prefix becomes a dict.get for the direction and an `elif words[0] in ["Min", "Max"]` for the setpoint, which removes the `prefix` variable; the template plus .format() becomes an f-string; `class_exists` is inlined into the `if not`; `len(definition[1])` becomes `definition[1]`; `open(Path(...))` becomes `open("...")`; `+=` for the setpoint suffix. Kept: the raise ValueError, both CSV guards, and the second query as a raw f-string (its `brick:{setpoint}` is a prefixed name pasted into SPARQL text, which no island expresses and which a Python-built IRI would not reproduce on a setpoint that is not a valid local name).

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph graph`; the three graph.add() become `+{ }`, with `f"{definition[1]}"@en` and `f"{limit_def}"@en` for Literal(..., lang="en") (strings, so the same literals) and `f<{definition[2]}>` for URIRef(definition[2]) (no @base in scope); the path loop becomes `m{ ?param {rdfs:subClassOf * "*"} brick:Limit }` (an interpolated rdflib path, same length as the Python selector); the alias test becomes `not m{ {param} brick:aliasOf [] }` (2 tokens shorter). No exception to the symmetry rule. The ldpy artefact is longer (ratio 1.036) because the translation's header declares 13 prefixes for 3 used.
